patch.value: Every public API route lacked rate limiting, leaving auth and write endpoints open to abuse and denial of service

CodeQL reported 161 open high-severity alerts on origin/main: 155 js/missing-rate-limiting across every router in src/routes plus the file-serving routes in src/app.ts, 2 js/missing-token-validation (CSRF), 1 js/tainted-format-string, 1 js/request-forgery, 1 js/polynomial-redos and 1 js/insufficient-password-hash. grep for rate/limit/throttle in src returned nothing and the Caddy reverse proxy declares no rate_limit, so the finding was real and unhandled at every layer: every route was unthrottled, including credential-checking auth routes. pm-web is a multi-tenant hosted service meant to carry thousands of concurrent users per project, so unthrottled auth and write routes are an abuse and availability risk, not a lint nit. This adds real per-route rate limiting (express-rate-limit) with distinct tiers keyed on the real client IP behind the proxy, a CSRF guard, and fixes for the format-string, request-forgery and ReDoS alerts.

value.author: codex
value.text: Measured on origin/main before any change: gh api --paginate repos/unbraind/pm-web/code-scanning/alerts?state=open&per_page=100 returned 161 open alerts, all high severity: 155 js/missing-rate-limiting (every router in src/routes plus /sw.js, the legal pages and the SPA fallback in src/app.ts), 2 js/missing-token-validation, 1 js/tainted-format-string, 1 js/request-forgery, 1 js/polynomial-redos, 1 js/insufficient-password-hash. grep -rniE rate.?limit|express-rate|throttle src returned nothing and Caddy declares no rate_limit, confirming the finding is real and unhandled at every layer.

value.author: codex
value.text: Tiers, not one global bucket. express-rate-limit is applied per mount in src/app.ts with five independent in-memory stores. Auth tier (20/min, all methods) guards /api/auth - credential brute-force; bcrypt cost 12 is about 250ms per attempt so 20/min/IP already costs about 5s of CPU, and legitimate users authenticate rarely (30-day session). Admin tier (30/min) guards /api/admin - privileged operations are rare in normal use. Read tier (600/min, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS only) and write tier (300/min, unsafe methods only) are a shared pair across every other API mount, split by HTTP method via the limiters skip predicate so reads and writes carry separate per-minute budgets. Static tier (600/min) guards the file-serving routes. A single human collaborating in real time stays well under 300 writes/min and 600 reads/min, so the limits stop scripted floods without throttling normal collaboration. All limits are overridable via PM_WEB_RATE_LIMIT_* env vars with these production defaults.

value.author: codex
value.text: Client identity behind the proxy is verified, not assumed. Express had no trust proxy setting, so req.ip was the proxy address and every client would share one bucket. createApp now sets app.set trust proxy from resolveTrustProxy (PM_WEB_TRUST_PROXY), defaulting to 1 hop for the documented Caddy deployment and never the boolean true which express-rate-limit refuses because it lets callers forge X-Forwarded-For. The integration test proves the keying: with trust proxy 1, requests with X-Forwarded-For 1.1.1.1 exhaust their bucket (429) while a request with X-Forwarded-For 2.2.2.2 gets its own bucket (200). If the limiter keyed on the proxy instead, the second request would also be 429.

value.author: codex
value.text: Other six alerts: js/polynomial-redos (auth.ts email regex) fixed by an isValidEmail helper that splits on the single @ and validates each side with anchored single-class patterns plus a 254-char bound, eliminating the quadratic backtracking on a no-@ string. js/request-forgery (github.ts issues URL) fixed by building the URL with new URL/URLSearchParams, whitelisting state to open/closed/all and clamping per_page/page, so no query value is interpolated raw. js/tainted-format-string (pm.ts console.error) fixed by using %s specifiers and passing the values as arguments instead of interpolating them into the format string. js/missing-token-validation x2 (CSRF) fixed by a real same-origin guard in src/csrf.ts that blocks provably cross-site cookie-authenticated mutations using the unforgeable Sec-Fetch-Site header with an Origin fallback, and issues a double-submit csrf_token cookie. js/insufficient-password-hash is a genuine false positive (a SHA-256 cache-key digest of the NEO4J_PASSWORD service credential used only to detect rotation, not password storage; the credential must be passed cleartext to neo4j.auth.basic) and is dismissed through the API with a written reason, not silenced inline.

patch.value: Implemented per-route tiered rate limiting keyed on the real client IP behind the proxy, a CSRF same-origin guard, and fixes for the ReDoS, SSRF and format-string alerts. All quality gates pass: build, typecheck, the full test suite (366 tests) and the coverage gate (68.99/81.75/64.01 over 29 source files, above the 66/80/60 thresholds), docstring gate (558 declarations documented), changelog:full and changelog:check, and pm health --strict-exit. The limiter tests were proven non-vacuous by reverting the middleware and watching them fail. js/insufficient-password-hash dismissed as a genuine false positive via the API.
